{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABdDUmHQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhGlo9M", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 235, "title": "Make Graph Editor canvas-first: compact toolbar, in-canvas zoom controls, and lean Inspector", "body": "## Problem

Graph Editor currently spends too much vertical room on **two separate full-width toolbars**:
- Main row: **Save graph**, graph/draft status, **Add Node**, **Graph actions**, **Help**.
- Second row: **Canvas zoom**, **Fit graph**, **Edit at 100%**.

This reduces the available canvas area. At the same time, the Inspector has redundant **Clear selection** and **This Node has no configurable settings.** UI, puts **Remove Node** at the bottom, and labels the node instance identifier ambiguously as **Node: `id`**.

**Goal:** prioritize an expansive, usable graph canvas while keeping frequent controls easy to access and making the Inspector more concise. Consistent with the shared Live/Graph/Models visual style (#229), and preserve the anchored Add Node quick-add behavior (#231).

## Intended layout

```text
Graph · Unsaved                         [+ Add Node] [Save] […] [?]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│  Graph canvas                               │ Settings            │
│                                             │     [Remove Node]   │
│              nodes and edges                │ Hold                │
│                                             │ Instance ID: hold-1 │
│                                             │ [Node help and ports]│
│ [−] [100%] [+] [Fit]                       │                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
```

This is a functional hierarchy, not a requirement for exact pixel values or fixed widths.

## A. Single compact Graph toolbar

- Consolidate primary graph controls into **one compact row**, eliminating the separate viewport-actions row above the canvas.
- Keep **Add Node** and **Save** immediately visible as high-frequency actions.
- Replace the verbose inline graph-state text with a concise **Saved / Unsaved** state indicator (and a clear conflict/active-earlier-graph indication when necessary). Do **not** suppress meaningful save/preparation errors or state warnings.
- Move the existing **Graph actions** commands (**Validate, Load saved, Reset, Import, Export, optional warning toggle**, etc.) into one accessible overflow **“…”** menu. Preserve all existing recovery and graph-action functions, confirmations and keyboard navigation.
- Make **Help** a compact **“?”** control with accessible label, retaining the existing Help dialog and focus handling.
- Preserve the existing **Add Node quick-add anchored to its trigger**, closing behavior, search, and click-to-add; repositioning must not make the popup appear off-screen.
- When horizontal space is constrained, favor **Add Node** and **Save**, putting lower-frequency controls into overflow rather than silently hiding them or wrapping into an unnecessary second toolbar row. Maintain touch targets and clear accessible names.

## B. In-canvas zoom and Fit

- Move **Canvas zoom**, **Fit graph**, and the useful parts of **Edit at 100%** from the second row to a **compact floating control group at the bottom-left (or equivalently unobtrusive corner) of the graph viewport**.
- Proposed controls: **− / current zoom % / + / Fit**; clicking the percent can present a zoom chooser or offer return to 100%. Preserve precise existing zoom options (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 125%, 150%) and custom Fit behavior. Do not regress smaller Fit scales or keyboard adjustment.
- Fold redundant **Edit at 100%** behavior into an obvious 100% reset while preserving its important *return focus to the edited element* capability.
- Keep the controls fixed in the viewport while the graph canvas pans/scrolls, not in the graph content itself; do not let canvas transforms scale the controls.
- Respect graph node/edge pointer interactions, selection, zoom anchoring, scroll extents, drag/detach/reconnect and routing. The controls must not obscure essential ports or make the last row of graph content unreachable.
- Add clear labels/tooltips and keyboard/touch support; responsive behavior at narrow viewport sizes.

## C. Simplify the right Inspector (agreed in same discussion)

- **Remove the `Clear selection` button entirely.** Escape and clicking blank canvas must still clear selection. Clicking an already selected node heading **again** should toggle its selection off; preserve dragging, keyboard and touch interactions.
- Move **Remove Node** from the bottom of Inspector to the upper action position formerly occupied by Clear selection, ideally aligned with the **Settings** heading. Use a clearly recognizable but restrained destructive-button treatment. Do not delete a node merely by selecting/deselecting it; existing graph mutation, undo/draft and focus semantics must remain correct.
- Show the type/name of the node and change **`Node: hold-1` → `Instance ID: hold-1`** (example). This is an **informational label only**; do not rename actual node IDs, alter graph JSON or connection identities.
- **Completely remove** the line `This Node has no configurable settings.` for Nodes with no configurable settings. Do not add empty filler sections or alternative placeholder explanations. Keep **Node help and ports** accessible as before.
- When a node does have settings, render its actual controls below the compact identity header as normal.
- For **edge selection**, keep actual connection detail and **Disconnect**; do not incorrectly show **Remove Node** when only an edge is selected. The unwanted Clear selection control should be absent in both modes.

## Likely implementation

- `extension/graph-editor.js`: toolbar construction, `viewportActions`, zoom/fit/focus, popovers, `drawInspector()`, selected-node heading click, keyboard and focus.
- `extension/recorder.css`, `extension/app.css`, `extension/graph.css` as appropriate for compact positioning and responsive behavior.
- Packaged extension/MV3 and UI regression tests covering layout, interaction and focus, plus Graph Editor help/docs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No standalone Canvas zoom / Fit graph toolbar row consuming vertical canvas space.
- [ ] One compact top bar displays Add Node and Save prominently; Graph actions are available via `…` and Help via `?`, with no lost functionality.
- [ ] Canvas zoom controls float within the **viewport** and stay put on pan/scroll; zoom at preset percentages and Fit works without breaking node placement, path routing or focus recovery.
- [ ] The available canvas area is measurably taller or less vertically obstructed than before at representative desktop and narrower sizes; controls don't overlap essential graph content.
- [ ] Inspector has **no Clear selection button**. Blank-canvas click, Esc, and repeated click on selected node heading provide intuitive deselection.
- [ ] Node Inspector shows **Remove Node near the top** and **Instance ID: `<id>`**, with actual settings when present.
- [ ] For nodes without settings, there is no `This Node has no configurable settings.` message or empty replacement; help and ports remain available.
- [ ] Edge selection still provides connection details and Disconnect, without inappropriate Node removal controls.
- [ ] Existing confirmation dialogs, graph actions, import/export, save/draft semantics, Add Node quick-add, editor selection/drag, zoom, keyboard and touch interactions remain correct.
- [ ] Tests and screenshots demonstrate the revised UI at typical desktop and narrow responsive widths; update help/documentation to describe changed controls and report tests actually executed.

## Scope

Graph Editor UX and layout only. No new node types, pipeline or graph execution changes, data migrations, or redesign of Live / Models.
